title: Managed Identities
description: Remove secrets entirely by using managed identities for Azure resource authentication.

data.text: Managed identities provide an Azure-managed identity for your App Service, VM, or Function. Instead of storing credentials, your code authenticates directly to Azure resources using the identity.

rows: Simple apps with one identity need
Shared identity across apps or VMs

data.text: Enable Managed Identity for App Service

data.title: Enable system-assigned managed identity
data.content: Use the Azure CLI to turn on managed identity for your App Service.
data.code:
az webapp identity assign \
  --name azure-for-aspnet-demo \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg

# Output contains the principalId
az webapp identity show \
  --name azure-for-aspnet-demo \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg

data.text: After enabling managed identity, assign Key Vault access policies or RBAC roles to the service principal so the app can read secrets without any credentials in code.

data.title: Assign Key Vault Secrets User role
data.content: Use Azure RBAC to grant the App Service identity permission to read secrets.
data.code:
$principalId = "$(az webapp identity show --name azure-for-aspnet-demo --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg --query principalId -o tsv)"

az role assignment create \
  --role "Key Vault Secrets User" \
  --assignee-object-id $principalId \
  --scope $(az keyvault show --name aspnet-azure-kv --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg --query id -o tsv)

data.text: When deployed to Azure, `DefaultAzureCredential` automatically uses the managed identity. Locally, it falls back to `AzureCliCredential`.

data.title: Same code works locally and in Azure
data.content: No connection string or client secret is required when using managed identity.

data.title: Remove secrets from local settings
data.description: After enabling managed identity, remove secrets from appsettings and run the app in Azure.
steps: Enable managed identity on the App Service
Grant Key Vault access to the managed identity
Deploy the app and verify it still reads secrets in Azure
data.expectedOutcome: The app works in Azure without any secret values in configuration files.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identities remove the need for client secrets or certificates
`DefaultAzureCredential` uses managed identity in Azure automatically
Grant access with Azure RBAC, not shared access policies
System-assigned identities are simplest; user-assigned identities are shared
data.takeaway: Managed identities are the Azure-native replacement for credentials. Once configured, your C# code never touches a secret string.
